speaker: Mr Desmond Choo
text: asked the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment in light of the recent flash floods in Singapore caused by the monsoon surges in recent months (a) whether the Ministry will consider conducting additional in-depth reviews on the adequacy of our drainage systems to deal with such monsoon surges; and (b) whether the current investments by the Government to improve drainage infrastructure are sufficient.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: In addition, I will address one written PQ filed by Miss Rachel Ong for the 4 February 2025 Sitting.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: These three PQs relate to the recent monsoon surges and drainage improvement efforts and with your permission, I will respond to these PQs together.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: In January this year, Singapore and the region experienced two monsoon surges which brought about prolonged rain.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: The first monsoon surge lasted four days from 10 January to 13 January, and the second monsoon surge lasted three days from 17 January to 19 January.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Over these two monsoon surges in January 2025, there was one incident of flooding, which occurred at Jalan Seaview.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Jalan Seaview is a low-lying area subject to tidal influence.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Since the 1980s, a tidal gate has been put in place in the outlet drain downstream of Jalan Seaview, to help mitigate tidal flood risks for this area.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: On 10 January, heavy rain coincided with high tide and this led to the flooding at the side road bend, a stretch of about 50 metres, of Jalan Seaview.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: The flooding on the road was about 0.3 metres and lasted close to three hours due to the high tide.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: The house next to this road experienced flooding within its car porch area.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Based on the Public Utilities Board's (PUB's) records, in the past five years, this is the only stretch of road along Jalan Seaview that has experienced flooding.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: While PUB had upgraded the roadside drains at Jalan Seaview in 2014 to increase their drainage capacity, some areas in the vicinity of Jalan Seaview are still susceptible to flooding as the road levels are marginally above the high tide level.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: The longer-term plan is to reclaim and build "Long Island" which will protect the East Coast area, including Jalan Seaview, from rising sea levels and tidal floods.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Agencies have initiated technical studies and are engaging the public and stakeholders to shape the plans for "Long Island".

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: We encourage developments in low-lying areas, including at Jalan Seaview, to put in place their own flood protection measures, such as deploying flood protection devices.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: To help residents and businesses, PUB has been issuing flood protection devices, such as flood barriers and inflatable sand bags, as part of the annual monsoon preparation and providing guidance on how to deploy these devices properly in a timely manner.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Climate change will increase flood risks in Singapore due to more extreme and unpredictable rainfall.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: PUB adopts a multi-pronged approach to enhance Singapore's flood resilience.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: We will spend about $150 million on these projects in FY2025.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: We are currently reviewing the drainage infrastructure plan for the next review cycle of FY2026 to 2030.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: That said, it is neither practical nor prudent in land-scarce Singapore to keep building more drains or expanding our drainage infrastructure.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Doing so, would require significant land and financial resources, which would then not be available for other important uses.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: To put things into perspective, flooding in Singapore is localised and typically subsides within an hour.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: It is, hence, more effective to build up flood resilience at a systems level, where building owners, developers, as well as the wider community, all play their part alongside the Government.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: To this end, PUB works closely with building owners and developers on measures that have to be taken at the individual development level to strengthen flood resilience.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: PUB's Code of Practice on Surface Water Drainage provides requirements on minimum platform and crest levels for buildings and flood protection measures that building owners and developers must implement to protect their premises.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Amendments to the Sewerage and Drainage Act were passed in November 2024 to ensure that owners and developers continue to operate and maintain the flood protection measures in their premises properly after implementation.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: PUB also proactively engages the community to better prepare for and respond to flood incidents.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: PUB works with the National Environment Agency (NEA) to forecast intense rainfall and issue early warning of potential floods to better prepare the public ahead of flood incidents.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: PUB launched its flood preparedness campaign "Get Flood-Wise" in November 2024 and worked with partners, such as Grab and BlueSG, to share flood readiness tips with drivers and commuters.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Managing flood risks is a collective effort between the Government, businesses and the public.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: I encourage everyone to play their part in enhancing Singapore's flood resilience.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: The first one is, because it will take some time for us to build "Long Island" or longer infrastructure improvements, so, what are the interim measures, including more pumps that can be deployed quickly, especially when we are going to expect more of such monsoon-type of weather events?

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: The second one is, we have committed to certain investments in the longer run.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Now that we start to see more frequent occurrences, do we expect to invest even more?

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: And if so, are we in a process of determining how much this would be?

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Indeed, I think we need to look at both short-term as well as long-term measures.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: I think in the short run, we would like to see how we can prepare the public including residents, better, faster and give them more effective means to protect themselves, including the availability of more devices to protect their own property.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Whether the pumps will be really effective in the case of Jalan Seaview, that may be doubtful because we are talking about the coincidence of both intense rain and high tide.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: So, it is difficult to pump something out if the tide is against you.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: What we really need to do is, where we can, for example, in Marina Barrage, we will start pumping ahead of time, prepare as much as we can, but still, more importantly is to get the local community, especially in the flood prone areas to be prepared themselves.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: So, awareness, public engagement, early warning, advising public to sign up to PUB's channel for information.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: In intense rain with high tide, as we have seen recently, we need to manage both together, and that is the reason why PUB is now the coastal protection agency.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: We are in the process of doing that.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: But the point that I like to make is that, even as we are able to foresee a greater occurrence of such extreme weather events, sometimes it is just not financially wise for us to prepare for the extreme events, because that will mean dedicating a lot of land, a lot of financial resources to protect us for those events that may not occur so regularly or in places where it does not occur regularly.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: It is still the same message, that while the Government will look at improving our infrastructure, we need community, we need businesses, we need owners to also undertake protection measures to protect themselves, protect their properties and protect their families.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: One is with regard to Minister's answer earlier, about the collaboration with NEA.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Can the Minister share how the Ministry intends to collaborate with other agencies to ensure a coordinated flood response in the future, if it gets too extreme, that sort of scenario?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Second is, I think, the Minister shared earlier about flood mitigation measures for housing and corporates or individuals.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Can the Minister share whether it is possible to have financial or logistical support available for residents and businesses affected by the floods and whether there can be budget allocation for future flood mitigation?

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: I think I have alluded in the earlier reply that we are working with NEA for better forecasts and also giving us more localised forecasts.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Because, I think, when it comes to flooding, it is very localised, especially in Singapore when our floods occur in very small areas.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: We are also working with LTA to try to get some of these traffic advisories out faster.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: For example, we are working to include some of these warning advisories in the ERP 2.0 so that we can receive the early warnings as we are driving.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: We are also working with the Singapore Police Force and the Singapore Civil Defence Force when it comes to emergencies related to floodings, in case there is a need to protect and save lives.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: So, there is close coordination between PUB and many related agencies.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: On the need for financial support, I would say that actually the measures that we are putting in place really start from a very basic design.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: So, when it comes to developers, for example, we are expecting them to start putting in some of these budgets so that they can plan the infrastructure, the protection measures, as and when they are planning.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: This will be reflected in the land price and also in the development costs that they will be including in their development plans.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: As to businesses as well as in the residential areas, I think PUB works very closely with them.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: In fact, over the years, we have been reducing the flood-prone areas significantly.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: I mean, when I was a child growing up, I remember that floods occurred in much wider areas more frequently, and many more businesses, including some in Chinatown, for example, quite regularly suffered from the impact of heavy rain and flooding.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: I think over the years, this has significantly been reduced.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: As and when they are needed, we will offer more help and we will keep a very close contact with the public and the businesses when it comes to engaging them on deployment of flood protection devices.
